inputs.sbc_source: Share-based compensation expense, cash flow statement: FY2025 10-K 33.7; 9M-2026 10-Q 22.7 vs 9M-2025 24.2 -> TTM 32.2. No combined equity-award figure published; award withholding taxes are immaterial and sit in financing 'Other'.
inputs.share_count_basis: 317.9m basic shares outstanding at 2026-09-30 (10-Q balance sheet: 317,902,668) plus ~1.6m dilutive awards (the basic-to-diluted spread in the last profitable quarters; Q3-2026 diluted equals basic only because of the loss). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. No buybacks since FY2024, so the flat count is a convention the company is not currently funding - immaterial at 0.27% of revenue.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Cost of equity ~10% (10-yr UST ~4.3% + beta ~1.15 x 5% ERP); pre-tax debt ~5.6% (the Aug-2026 notes priced 5.35-5.90%), ~4.2% after tax; at a 70/30 target structure WACC ~8.3%, rounded to 8.5%. One rate for all three scenarios - cyclicality and input-cost risk are carried in the flows and the weights, not a WACC premium. Terminal cap 14x FCF (cyclical band 12-15x); it binds below Gordon (15.7x at 8.5%/2%).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases are already expensed inside EBITDA (treatment B); operating lease obligations of 211.9 are excluded from net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100% of Miski Mayo); non-controlling interests are deducted once in the equity bridge at ~10x normal NCI distributions/earnings (~30/yr), about 2x the 149.3 book value.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF with mid-cycle normalisation (dcf-methods routing: cyclical operating company, owner-fcf.md + adaptations). Fresh build, no prior valuation. FY0 is the trailing twelve months to 30-Sep-2026 so the flows start where the balance sheet stops; year 1 (Oct-26 to Sep-27) contains the guided Q4-2026 trough. EBITDA is defined as operating earnings + DD&A + impairments/idling charges, i.e. AFTER asset-retirement accretion - lower than management's adjusted EBITDA. On that definition: TTM ~1,250 (10.5% margin; 9M-2026 = -505.0 + 900.6 + ~496 of Araxa/Patrocinio/Carlsbad charges), FY2025 ~17%, FY2023-24 ~17-20%, FY2018-20 ~14-19%, FY2021-22 27-30%; the FY2018-25 average is 20.7% including the 2021-22 supercycle and 16.8% excluding it. Base mid-cycle 18.5% sits between. NET DEBT: short-term debt 511.6 + current maturities 68.7 + long-term debt 5,332.8 = 5,913.1 less cash 272.6. BRIDGE: Ma'aden shares at Tadawul fair value added (their mark-to-market is in other income, outside EBITDA); structured accounts payable deducted as debt-like; NCI deducted. ARO (2,529.7 on balance sheet) is charged in the FLOWS, not the bridge: accretion is inside EBITDA and cash spend above accretion (~100/yr) is inside the capex line; the RCRA trusts (~751, restricted to gypstack closure) are therefore left out of the bridge too. Reported FCF is levered (after ~200 of interest paid) and TTM is depressed by the trough plus a working-capital unwind, so last_fcf is not a base to grow from - the forward flows are built from components. Interest income not stripped (net debt, not net cash). Working capital consumes cash on growth (receivables + inventory exceed payables): capture -15%. Price is a regular-session close.
warnings: TTM owner FCF is negative (-840.5); the valuation rests entirely on mid-cycle margin recovery.
Bear scenario: enterprise value is below net debt - equity is worth nothing on that path absent the Ma'aden stake. See valuation_philosophy.
Hurdle entry prices are negative in base and bear: at a 15% required return the mid-cycle flows do not cover net debt, so no price meets the hurdle unless the bull case plays out (bull entry 8.40).

scenario_narratives.base: Q4-2026 is the trough as guided: sulfur at 800-850/lt in COGS, phosphate operating rate near 50%. Cheaper contracted sulfur reaches COGS through 2027 and DAP prices give back part of the cost-push rise, so revenue is flat-to-down while the stripping margin rebuilds. Margin recovers 13% -> 17% -> 18.5% mid-cycle, between the 16.8% ex-supercycle and 20.7% all-in FY2018-25 averages. Araxa, Carlsbad and Taquari leaving the portfolio lets capex drift from ~1.3bn to ~1.1-1.15bn plus ~100 of ARO cash. Potash stays well supplied at ~280/t. Mature unlevered owner FCF ~650-700, in line with the FY2018-25 record.
scenario_narratives.bull: The sulfur shock leaves phosphate structurally tight: Chinese export restraint persists, US countervailing duties on Moroccan/Russian product survive litigation, and Florida/Louisiana runs back above 65% utilisation at high stripping margins. Potash firms as Belarus volumes stay logistically constrained. Mid-cycle margin 22% (the FY2018-25 average including 2021-22 is 20.7%), the pruned portfolio holds capex under 10% of sales, and Brazil distribution recovers with farmer credit.
scenario_narratives.bear: Sulfur and ammonia stay elevated on Hormuz/Kazakhstan disruption while affordability destroys phosphate demand (management already sees shipments down ~20mt), so price cannot outrun cost. New potash supply (Belarus sanction relief, greenfield tonnes) pushes MOP back toward 220-240/t; Chinese low-analysis phosphate keeps taking Brazilian share. Margin settles at 15%, below the 16.8% ex-supercycle average, with trapped losses keeping the cash tax rate high. On this path enterprise value does not cover ~5.6bn of net debt and the investment-grade rating and dividend are at risk.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: leverage has just stepped up (debt 3.4bn -> 5.9bn in seven quarters) into negative free cash flow, and the bear path is a balance-sheet problem, not just lower margins. Base 50%: management's trough-and-recover guidance plus the long-run margin record. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs phosphate tightness, CVD survival and a benign potash market together, and fertilizer supercycle margins have historically lasted two years.
probability_weighted.limited_liability_note: The engine weights the bear case at its computed -6.04/share (EV below net debt). Equity cannot be worth less than zero; with the bear floored at 0 the weighted value is 13.25 rather than 11.74. The unfloored figure is kept as the canonical weighted_iv because it is the engine's output and the more conservative of the two; the negative is best read as the size of the recapitalisation the bear path would need (~1.9bn).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mosaic is valued on normalised mid-cycle cash flow, not on the trough it is in or the 2022 peak. The awkward fact is cash conversion: capex plus reclamation absorbs roughly half of mid-cycle EBITDA and cash taxes are heavy because Canadian potash profits cannot be sheltered by US/Brazilian losses, so ~2.2bn of mid-cycle EBITDA becomes only ~650-700 of unlevered owner FCF - which matches what the company actually produced over FY2018-25. Against ~5.6bn of net debt that leaves equity as a geared residual: small changes in the mid-cycle margin move per-share value several-fold, and the Ma'aden stake is a large share of what is left.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle EBITDA margin is the whole valuation: each 1pp is worth roughly US$3/share at this leverage
Sustaining capex: if the pruned portfolio really runs on ~1.0bn rather than ~1.15bn + ARO, base value rises materially
Ma'aden stake (1.79bn at 30-Sep-2026) is taken at quoted value with no tax, lock-up or block discount
Leverage: net debt 5.6bn plus 0.4bn structured payables against TTM EBITDA of ~1.25bn; a prolonged trough forces asset sales, a dividend cut or equity
ARO of 2.5bn is carried in the flows at ~100/yr above accretion; a regulatory step-up in gypstack closure spending is not modelled
The 14x terminal cap binds in every scenario; at 12x base value falls by roughly US$1.5-2/share
